body.text: How do entry prices, rental yield and liquidity compare in 2026?

In 2026, Istanbul averages roughly TRY 63,788 per square meter with gross rental yields between 7.1% and 7.7%, Antalya averages about TRY 55,264 per square meter with steady expat demand, and Bodrum commands the highest luxury entry prices while delivering lower net yields around 3.2% due to seasonality and upkeep.

Liquidity separates these markets sharply. Per [Emlak Platform's 2026 city data](https://www.emlakplatform.com.tr/en/articles/how-to-choose-the-right-city-for-real-estate-investment) and [Bosphorus Brokers' Istanbul guide](https://www.bosphorusbrokers.com/guides/rental-income-in-istanbul/), compact 1+1 and 2+1 flats in Şişli, Ataşehir, and Kadıköy attract deep domestic tenant pools, netting 4.1% to 6.5%. Conversely, [Investropa's 2026 yield dataset](https://investropa.com/blogs/news/turkey-rental-yields) and [RestProperty's Bodrum guide](https://restproperty.com/article-en/statioturcii/bodrum-area-guide-2026-living-real-estate-districts/) show Bodrum acting as a lifestyle market with 2%–4% typical gross yields and ~3.2% net on larger villas.
Which city works best for $400K citizenship vs lifestyle second home?

Istanbul and Antalya are the most practical hubs for the $400,000 Turkish Citizenship by Investment program because both offer liquid residential units near the threshold, whereas Bodrum suits buyers prioritizing a summer lifestyle home and willing to spend well above $400,000 for limited-supply coastal land.

Under the [Invest in Türkiye property framework](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/acquiring-property-and-citizenship.aspx), acquiring at least $400,000 USD in qualifying real estate with a three-year no-sale annotation supports citizenship eligibility. In Istanbul, $400,000 buys a liquid 2+1 near transit or two smaller flats. In Antalya, it often secures a larger Konyaaltı or Lara residence. Prime Bodrum zones like Yalıkavak and Türkbükü routinely exceed $600,000, favoring personal lifestyle use.
How do earthquake risk, short-term rental laws and closed Ikamet districts compare?

All three cities require parcel-level checks against AFAD's earthquake hazard map, strict compliance with Law No. 7464 for stays under 100 days, and address verification for residence permits, as Istanbul lifted closed-neighborhood bans in June 2026 while Antalya still applies selective local address scrutiny.
Check these three compliance pillars before committing capital:

items: Seismic safety and DASK: Verify the parcel on the [AFAD Earthquake Hazard Map](https://en.afad.gov.tr/turkeys-new-earthquake-hazard-map-is-published), confirm post-2018 code compliance, and check [DASK earthquake insurance](https://www.dask.gov.tr/en/tariffs-and-premiums).

Short-term rental permits (Law No. 7464): Per [Rona Legal's Law 7464 guide](https://www.ronalegal.com/en/blog/turkey-airbnb-law-7464-short-term-rental-permit), rentals of 100 days or fewer require a Ministry of Culture and Tourism permit and unanimous building-owner consent.

Residence permits (Ikamet): Under [Presidency of Migration Management rules](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types) and [2026 residency updates](https://www.ronalegal.com/en/blog/residence-permit-turkey-foreigners), property-based residency requires a $200,000 USD recorded valuation; Istanbul reopened closed districts in June 2026, while Antalya still requires street-level checks.

faq.q: Can one $400,000 property qualify for Turkish citizenship in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, provided it meets official valuation, title deed, and Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate rules and is held for three years. Multiple qualifying units can also be combined.

faq.q: Do I need a Tourism Rental Permit for Airbnb in Istanbul, Bodrum, or Antalya?
faq.a: Yes. Under Law No. 7464, residential leases of 100 days or fewer require a Ministry of Culture and Tourism permit plus unanimous building-owner consent in apartment blocks.

faq.q: Are Istanbul neighborhoods still closed to foreign residence permits?
faq.a: Istanbul lifted closed-neighborhood bans across city districts in June 2026, though rules shift frequently and Antalya still applies localized scrutiny. Always verify your exact address with a Turkish lawyer.

faq.q: What is the minimum property value for a residence permit (Ikamet) in 2026?
faq.a: A property-based short-term residence permit requires a residential property valued at $200,000 USD or more, officially recorded on the title deed and backed by a Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate.

faq.q: Which city offers the highest net rental yield in 2026?
faq.a: Compact 1+1 and 2+1 flats in central Istanbul districts like Şişli, Ataşehir, and Kadıköy typically deliver stronger net yields (roughly 4.1% to 6.5%) than seasonal Bodrum villas (~3.2%).
